ds: A cleric who inscribes divine runes onto surfaces and allies, turning the battlefield into a sacred text.
Clerics of storm and sea.
Clerics of mischief and deception.
Clerics who guard the night — protectors against darkness and despair.
Clerics of battle gods.
Druids tied to the fey realm of dreams.
A druid who tends decay the way others tend growth, wielding withering touch and spreading spore clouds.
Druids who embrace decay as part of the natural cycle.

Circle of Stars expands the fantasy and gameplay style of the Druid class.
 This subclass focuses on a unique identity, combat role, and spell progression.
Druids of destructive and renewing flame.
A druid balanced between a light aspect and a dark one, shifting stance to change what their Wild Shape carries.
A druid bonded to a specific terrain, drawing extra spells and resilience from the land itself rather than from an animal bond.
Druids who master Wild Shape for combat.
Druids of ocean and storm, carrying the sea's fury with them. (Player's Handbook (2024))
Druids who speak for the wild and lead summoned animals and fey.
A druid attuned to the raw power of storms — lightning, wind, and the chaos of the tempest.
A druid who has become a prophet of natural law, reading the future in the behaviour of animals and plants.
A warrior who has sworn fealty to demonic powers, their armour and weapons corrupted by abyssal energy.
Elite archers who weave magic into their arrows.
A battlefield leader wreathed in ash and embers, whose banner and burnt ground punish anyone who gets close.
Knights who inspire and rally allies. (Printed in SCAG under a setting-specific name; later reprinted as Banneret.)
A martial tactician with a pool of combat maneuvers.
A fighter who protects allies and controls the battlefield, often on horseback.
The simplest and most consistent Fighter subclass — raw physical excellence rather than a trick or a resource to manage.
A fighter who has studied the art of killing to its absolute limit, understanding exactly how to end life most efficiently.
Fighters who summon echoes of themselves from other timelines.
A fighter who supplements martial skill with wizard spells.
A fighter who has sworn an oath to a dark power, combining martial prowess with hexes and curses.
A heavy-armor fighter built to hold a line rather than break one, intercepting blows meant for allies.
Fighters who augment strikes with psionic power.
Fighters who carve giant runes into their gear.
Warriors of unbreakable resolve.
A fighter touched by the Void rather than trained by any order, striking through resistance and folding space to close distance.
A monk who channels elemental energy through their body, each strike carrying the force of the elements.
A monk who has trained their body beyond its natural limits, turning flesh and bone into weapons harder than iron.
A monk trained in desert combat traditions, using dust, wind, and disorientation as weapons.
A monk who leaves an afterimage of every motion, doubling strikes and briefly fighting alongside their own echo.
Monks who wear masks and act as both healers and executioners.
A monk who breaks things rather than redirects them, fracturing armor and shattering already-wounded foes.
Monks trained in stealth, darkness, and infiltration.
Monks who emulate dragons.
Monks who manifest an astral form of their own body.
Monks with an unpredictable, swaying style.
A monk who trains around having nothing left to hold onto, immune to being grappled, restrained, or disarmed.
Monks who bend elemental forces through ki.
Monks who master specific weapons.
